name: Behavior Change Strategies
description: Practical intervention strategies for changing or reinforcing user behavior. Covers three strategic pillars: supporting conscious action (education, reflection), cheating (defaults, incidental design), and habit formation/disruption (automate new behaviors, replace existing routines). Designers select strategies by diagnosing the user's current behavioral state and target outcome.

subskills.name: Support Conscious Action — Educate & Encourage
subskills.description: Providing users with information, reasoning, and motivational framing to consciously adopt a new behavior. Includes onboarding walkthroughs, contextual tooltips, achievement celebrations, progress disclosure, and persuasive copywriting that addresses the user's why.

subskills.name: Support Conscious Action — Help User Think About Action
subskills.description: Prompting users to reflect on a potential action before taking it. Techniques include implementation intentions (if-then planning), commitment devices, reflection prompts, self-monitoring tools, and reminders that surface at decision-relevant moments.

subskills.name: Cheating — Defaulting
subskills.description: Designing the system so the desired behavior is the path of least resistance — the default. Users who take no action automatically end up in the preferred state. Covers opt-in vs opt-out defaults, pre-selected options, smart default settings, and automatic enrollment.

subskills.name: Cheating — Making It Incidental
subskills.description: Embedding the desired behavior into an existing action the user already performs, so it happens automatically without conscious effort. Examples include step counting that happens by carrying a phone, or saving money that happens automatically with each purchase.

subskills.name: Make/Change Habits — Automate Repetition (New Behavior)
subskills.description: Reducing the cognitive load of a new behavior until it becomes automatic through repetition scaffolding. Techniques include scheduled reminders, streak mechanics, habit stacking prompts, and progressive disclosure that reduces complexity over time as the habit forms.

subskills.name: Make/Change Habits — Modify Existing Behavior
subskills.description: Strategies for modifying established habits in the existing behavior → Avoid the Cue (remove environmental triggers), Replace the Routine (substitute behavior while keeping the same cue and reward), Use Consciousness/Mindfulness (bring automatic behaviors to conscious awareness), and Crowd Out Old Habit (replace it by building a competing positive habit).

junior.description: Designs clear onboarding and informational flows, and applies opt-out/opt-in defaults with proper rationale.

mid.description: Designs implementation intention prompts, embeds incidental behaviors, and scaffolds habit formation with streak mechanics and spaced repetition.

senior.description: Diagnoses entrenched behavioral patterns and selects the appropriate disruption strategy (avoid cue, replace routine, mindfulness, crowd out), with ethical evaluation of intervention strength.
